title: Sgt Credland Memorial, St Andrew's Church, Billingborough
location_name: St Andrew's Church, Billingborough, Lincolnshire, England
memorial_details: St Andrew's Church, Billingborough, contains a stone WW2 roll of honour tablet (seven names) and at least three private memorials. One private memorial is specifically dedicated to Sgt Ralph Hilton Credland RAFVR, son of Arthur and Rose A. Credland of Billingborough. The project seed describes the memorial as a font cover — this form of memorial is known in Lincolnshire churches of the period, but the attribution has not been confirmed from open sources and requires a site visit or access to church records. Sgt Credland is commemorated on the Runnymede Air Forces Memorial, indicating no known grave.
contributor: Keith Binley, Bomber Command Memorial Register
cause_of_loss: Believed ditched in the Moray Firth; empty dinghy found
narrative:
Sgt Ralph Hilton Credland RAFVR was among the crew of Wellington HF858 of 20 OTU, based at RAF Lossiemouth, which was lost on 28 January 1943. The aircraft is believed to have ditched in the Moray Firth; an empty dinghy was found. Credland has no known grave and is commemorated on the Runnymede Air Forces Memorial, Surrey. His parents arranged for a private memorial to be placed in St Andrew's Church, Billingborough.

Date confirmed as 28 January 1943 per Chorley Bomber Command Losses Vol 7 (cited in Facebook post by admin Tony Hibberd, RAF Bomber Command Memorials group). The unit and serial (20 OTU / HF858) are also from that source. The form of the private memorial — described as a font cover in the project's research notes — requires a site visit to confirm.
date_note: Date resolved to 28 January 1943. A previous discrepancy between 1942 and 1943 arose from an error in one secondary source. Chorley BCL Vol 7 gives 28/01/43 and is the more authoritative source.
community_connection: Private memorial placed by the Credland family. St Andrew's Church maintains the memorial.
